title: Mercury and the Tradesmen
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: When Jupiter was creating man, he told Mercury to make an infusion of lies, and to add a little of it to the other ingredients which went to the making of the Tradesmen. Mercury did so, and introduced an equal amount into each in turn--the tallow-chandler, and the greengrocer, and the haberdasher, and all, till he came to the horse-dealer, who was last on the list, when, finding that he had a quantity of the infusion still left, he put it all into him. This is why all Tradesmen lie more or less, but they none of them lie like a horse-dealer.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who told Mercury to make an infusion of lies?
options: Jupiter
The horse-dealer
The tallow-chandler
A council of tradesmen

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was Mercury told to add the infusion to?
options: The water supply of the city
The other ingredients used in making the Tradesmen
The food of every animal
The soil of the fields

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how much of the infusion did Mercury give each tradesman at first?
options: An equal amount into each in turn
None at all until the very end
Twice as much as the last one received
Only a trace amount to a chosen few

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who was last on Mercury's list of tradesmen?
options: The greengrocer
The haberdasher
The tallow-chandler
The horse-dealer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Mercury do with the infusion still left when he reached the horse-dealer?
options: He threw it away
He put it all into him
He saved it for the next batch of men
He divided it among the earlier tradesmen

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "infusion" mean in "an infusion of lies"?
options: A written contract
A mixture steeped or blended into something else
A loud argument
A form of punishment

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the horse-dealer end up with more of the infusion than the other tradesmen?
options: Jupiter specifically ordered Mercury to favor him
Being last on the list, he received whatever quantity of the mixture happened to remain
He asked Mercury for extra because he wanted an advantage
He was created separately from the other tradesmen

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable's closing line?
options: Only horse-dealers among tradesmen ever tell lies
All tradesmen lie somewhat, but horse-dealers are said to lie the most
Jupiter regrets creating tradesmen at all
Mercury refused to give any tradesman the infusion of lies

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who carried out the task of adding the infusion to the tradesmen?
options: Jupiter himself
Mercury
The horse-dealer
An unnamed servant

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which tradesmen are named before the horse-dealer?
options: The tallow-chandler, the greengrocer, and the haberdasher
The blacksmith, the baker, and the tanner
The weaver, the potter, and the mason
The fisherman, the farmer, and the miller

questions.prompt: According to the passage's final line, how do most tradesmen compare to a horse-dealer in lying?
options: They lie about the same amount as a horse-dealer
They lie more or less, but none like a horse-dealer
They never lie at all, unlike the horse-dealer
They lie more than a horse-dealer does

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "quantity" mean in "he had a quantity of the infusion still left"?
options: A type or variety
An amount
A price
A container

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the fable using the story of Mercury's task to explain?
options: Why Jupiter created different professions
Why horse-dealers, in particular, have a reputation for dishonesty
Why lying is considered a serious crime
Why Mercury became the god of trade

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Mercury distributes an infusion of lies evenly to all tradesmen, and none receives extra
Mercury shares out an infusion of lies among tradesmen, but the leftover all goes to the last one, the horse-dealer
Jupiter forbids Mercury from giving any tradesman the infusion of lies
The horse-dealer refuses his share of the infusion out of pride
